title: Strict reduction and normalized realization of completed open extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$, $T=U,X$, and identify $j^{-1}\widehat R_X=\widehat R_U$. Use the strict semilinear system category, reduction/total-limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $J_j$ be exact termwise system extension by zero, and let $j_!$ be localized ringed-site extension by zero for the completed coefficient sheaves [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

For any derived-complete $K\in D(\widehat R_U)$, with completeness meaning the quotient-tower condition of [def-weil-derived-complete], extension by zero on a flat-term K-flat reduction representative induces a specified natural isomorphism of derived semilinear systems
$$r_j(K):\mathcal R_X(j_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_UK.$$
Its evaluation at $n$ is the canonical open-tensor coefficient isomorphism $(j_!K)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X\cong j_!(K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_U}(A_n)_U)$, and it respects every strict quotient transition. The object $j_!K$ is derived complete. If $u_{j_!K}$ denotes the actual reduction/total-limit unit, then it is invertible and
$$d_j(K)=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(r_j(K))^{-1}:\mathcal L_XJ_j\mathcal R_UK\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!K.$$
With the corresponding completed restriction pullback, this comparison identifies the realized open adjunction unit and counit with the localized ringed-site unit and counit. These are comparisons of the specified simultaneous section constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], not choices of lifts of their evaluations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus] with $W=U$ and $W=X$, on which $\ell$ is invertible. It concerns the same strict semilinear system category, the same specified adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] with actual unit $u$ and counit $e$, the same normalized systems and the derived completeness of [def-weil-derived-complete]. It gives: on complete objects the actual $u$ is invertible, on normalized systems the actual $e$ is invertible, and reduction and total limit restrict to inverse equivalences between complete objects and normalized systems. In particular reduction of a complete object is normalized and total limit of a normalized system is complete. No boundedness or constructibility assumption occurs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-open-quotient-koszul-completeness] to the given $R,t,j,K$. Its coefficient identification and strict augmentation equality identify quotient completion with the actual unit. Since $j$ is quasi-compact and $K$ is quotient-complete, it gives quotient completeness of $j_!K$ and invertibility of the actual $u_{j_!K}$. Thus the preservation hypothesis needed below holds for every complete input.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model] to $K$. It supplies $r_j(K)$ as one specified strict semilinear chain comparison on flat-term K-flat representatives. Its coefficient components are the required canonical tensor isomorphisms and commute with every quotient transition before localization. Naturality and independence are part of this cited statement. Normalization from Step 1 therefore also holds for $J_j\mathcal R_UK$.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sf-open-reduction-adjunction-transport] now hold: Step 1 supplies the actual-unit/counit inverses and completeness of total limits, Step 2 supplies preservation by $j_!$, and Step 3 supplies precisely its required generator-normalized $r$. That lemma gives completed restriction and $s$, and the isomorphism $d_j(K)=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(r_j(K))^{-1}$, with its reduction normalization. Its system and realized unit/counit equations identify the realized open adjunction with the localized ringed-site adjunction. All comparisons use the specified simultaneous section constructions, as required.
